summary: Seven days before Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol moves out of his house into a special room in the Beis HaMikdash. Another Kohen is made ready in case he cannot serve.

chunks.he: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים קֹדֶם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַפְרִישִׁין
chunks.en: Seven days before Yom Kippur, they separate
chunks.st: Seven days prior to Yom Kippur the Sages would

words.note: Yom Kippur is the holiest day of the year, a day of fasting and teshuvah.

chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol from his house to the Parhedrin room.
chunks.st: remove the High Priest, who performs the entire Yom Kippur service, from his house to the Chamber of Parhedrin,
chunks.stMore: a room in the Temple designated specifically for the High Priest during that period.

words.note: Kohanim are the family of Aharon who served in the Beis HaMikdash.
The Kohen Gadol is the head Kohen, who does the whole service of Yom Kippur.
A room in the Beis HaMikdash where the Kohen Gadol stayed before Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And they get another Kohen ready to take his place,
chunks.st: And they would designate another priest in his stead to replace him

chunks.en: in case something happens that makes him unfit.
chunks.explain: For example, if he became tamei and could not go into the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: lest a disqualification due to impurity or another circumstance beyond his control prevent him from entering the Temple on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: they even get another wife ready for him,
chunks.st: The Sages would even designate another wife for him

chunks.en: in case his wife dies,
chunks.st: lest his wife die,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 16), "And he will atone
chunks.st: as it is stated in the Torah portion of the Yom Kippur service: “And it will atone

chunks.en: for himself and for his house."
chunks.st: for him and for his house” (Leviticus 16:6);

chunks.en: "His house" means his wife.
chunks.explain: The Kohen Gadol has to be married to do the Yom Kippur service.
chunks.st: the Sages interpreted the term: His house, that is his wife.
chunks.stMore: The priest must be married in order to fulfill this commandment. Due to the concern lest his wife die, another wife was designated to address that possibility.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: "If so,
chunks.st: If so, that this is a concern,

chunks.en: there will be no end to it!"
chunks.explain: The second wife might die too, so we don't worry about this.
chunks.st: there is no end to the matter,
chunks.stMore: as what if the designated replacement wife dies? This possibility need not be a source of concern.

summary: During the seven days, the Kohen Gadol practices the service by doing the daily avodah himself. All year long he may bring any korban he wants and take any part he chooses.

chunks.he: כָּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
chunks.en: All seven days he sprinkles the blood,
chunks.st: During all seven days of the High Priest’s sequestering before Yom Kippur, he sprinkles the blood of the daily burnt-offering,

chunks.en: and burns the ketores,
chunks.st: and he burns the incense,

words.note: A special mix of sweet-smelling spices burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and cleans the lamps of the Menorah,
chunks.st: and he removes the ashes of the lamps of the candelabrum,

chunks.en: and brings the head and the leg of the korban.
chunks.st: and he sacrifices the head and the hind leg of the daily offering.
chunks.stMore: The High Priest performs these tasks in order to grow accustomed to the services that he will perform on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And on all the other days,
chunks.st: On all the other days of the year,

chunks.en: if he wants to bring a korban, he brings it,
chunks.st: if the High Priest wishes to sacrifice any of the offerings, he sacrifices them,

chunks.en: because the Kohen Gadol brings a part first
chunks.st: as the High Priest sacrifices any portion that he chooses first

chunks.en: and takes a part first.
chunks.explain: He may pick whichever korban or portion he wants, before the other Kohanim.
chunks.st: and takes any portion that he chooses first.

summary: Elders of the beis din read the order of the Yom Kippur service with the Kohen Gadol. The day before Yom Kippur, they show him the animals he will bring, so he will be used to them.

chunks.he: מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: Elders from the beis din were given to him,
chunks.st: The Sages provided the High Priest with Elders selected from the Elders of the court,

words.note: Beis din is the court of Torah judges, here the great Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: and they read to him the order of the day.
chunks.explain: They read the part of the Torah about the Yom Kippur service.
chunks.st: and they would read before him the order of the service of the day of Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: And they say to him,
chunks.st: And they would say to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: read it yourself, with your own mouth,
chunks.st: Read the order of the service with your own mouth,

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא שָׁכַחְתָּ אוֹ שֶׁמָּא לֹא לָמָדְתָּ.
chunks.en: in case you forgot, or in case you never learned it."
chunks.st: as perhaps you forgot this reading or perhaps you did not learn to read.

chunks.en: On the morning before Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: On Yom Kippur eve in the morning,

chunks.en: they stand him at the eastern gate,
chunks.st: the Elders stand him at the eastern gate of the courtyard

chunks.en: and pass before him bulls, rams and sheep,
chunks.st: and pass before him bulls and rams and sheep

chunks.en: so that he will know them and be used to the service.
chunks.st: so that he will be familiar with the animals and grow accustomed to the service,
chunks.stMore: as these were the animals sacrificed on Yom Kippur.

summary: The Kohen Gadol may eat and drink what he wants during the seven days. But on the evening before Yom Kippur he may not eat much, so he will not fall asleep.

chunks.en: All seven days, they did not
chunks.st: Throughout all the seven days that the High Priest was in the Parhedrin chamber,

chunks.en: keep food and drink away from him.
chunks.st: they would not withhold from him any food or drink that he desired.

chunks.en: On the eve of Yom Kippur, when it got dark,
chunks.st: However, on Yom Kippur eve at nightfall,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ לֶאֱכֹל הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: they did not let him eat a lot,
chunks.st: they would not allow him to eat a great deal

chunks.en: because food brings sleep.
chunks.explain: He had to stay awake all night, as the next mishnayos explain.
chunks.st: because food induces sleep
chunks.stMore: and they did not allow him to sleep, as will be explained.

summary: The elders bring the Kohen Gadol to the Kohanim elders and make him promise to do the service exactly as they taught him. Then everyone cries.

chunks.he: מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: The elders of the beis din handed him over to the elders of the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The Elders of the court who read the order of the service of the day before the High Priest passed him to the Elders of the priesthood,

chunks.en: and they brought him up to the upper room of Beis Avtinas,
chunks.st: and they took him up to the House of Avtinas.

words.note: The family that made the ketores; they had a room in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and made him swear, and took leave of him, and went away.
chunks.st: And they administered him an oath and took leave of him and went on their way.

chunks.en: And they said to him,
chunks.st: When they administered this oath they said to him:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: we are messengers of the beis din,
chunks.st: We are agents of the court,

chunks.en: and you are our messenger and the messenger of the beis din.
chunks.st: and you are our agent and the agent of the court.

chunks.en: We make you swear by the One
chunks.st: We administer an oath to you in the name of

chunks.en: who made His Name rest in this House,
chunks.explain: That is Hashem, Whose Name rests in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: Him who housed His name in this House,

chunks.en: that you will not change anything at all
chunks.st: that you will not change even one matter from all

chunks.en: of what we told you."
chunks.explain: They worried he might do the ketores the wrong way.
chunks.st: that we have said to you
chunks.stMore: with regard to the burning of the incense or any other service that you will perform when alone.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains they feared he might follow the Tzedukim's wrong way.

chunks.en: He turns away and cries,
chunks.st: After this oath, he would leave them and cry,

chunks.en: and they turn away and cry.
chunks.explain: They were sad that they had to worry he might do it wrong.
chunks.st: and they would leave him and cry in sorrow that the oath was necessary.

summary: On the night of Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol stays awake learning Torah or hearing it read, so that he will not fall asleep.
stIntro: They kept him occupied throughout the night to prevent him from sleeping.

chunks.en: If he was a wise scholar,
chunks.st: If he was a scholar, he would

chunks.en: he teaches Torah. And if not,
chunks.st: teach Torah. If he was not a scholar,

chunks.en: Torah scholars teach before him.
chunks.st: Torah scholars would teach Torah before him.

chunks.en: And if he is used to reading,
chunks.st: And if he was accustomed to read the Bible,

chunks.en: he reads. And if not,
chunks.st: he would read; and if he was not,

chunks.en: they read before him.
chunks.st: they would read the Bible before him.

chunks.en: And what do they read before him?
chunks.st: And what books would they read before him to pique his interest so that he would not fall asleep? They would read

chunks.en: From Iyov, from Ezra and from Divrei HaYamim.
chunks.explain: These books are interesting, so they keep him awake.
chunks.st: from Job, and from Ezra, and from Chronicles.

words.note: Divrei HaYamim is the book of Chronicles.

chunks.en: Zecharyah ben Kevutal says,
chunks.st: Zekharya, son of Kevutal, says:

chunks.en: "Many times I read before him from Daniel."
chunks.st: Many times I read before him from the book of Daniel.

summary: If the Kohen Gadol starts to doze, the young Kohanim snap their fingers and tell him to stand on the cold floor, and they keep him busy until morning.

chunks.en: If he wanted to doze off,
chunks.st: If the High Priest sought to sleep at night,

chunks.he: פִּרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה מַכִּין לְפָנָיו בְּאֶצְבַּע צְרֵדָה,
chunks.en: the young Kohanim snap their fingers before him,
chunks.st: the young priests would snap the middle [tzerada] finger against the thumb before him,

chunks.en: and they say to him,
chunks.st: and they would say to him every so often:

chunks.en: "My master, Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: My Master, High Priest.

chunks.en: get up and cool yourself once on the floor."
chunks.explain: Standing on the cold stone floor would wake him up.
chunks.st: Stand from your bed and chill yourself once on the floor and overcome your drowsiness.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲסִיקִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ זְמַן הַשְּׁחִיטָה:
chunks.en: And they keep him busy until the time of the shechitah comes.
chunks.st: And they would engage him in various ways until the time would arrive to slaughter the daily offering.

words.note: The shechitah here is of the morning korban tamid.

summary: Every day the ashes are taken off the mizbeach around the time the rooster crows. On Yom Kippur this is done from midnight, and on Yamim Tovim even earlier.

chunks.en: Every day they clear the ashes from the mizbeach
chunks.st: Every day the priests would remove the ashes from the altar and place them on the east side of the ramp

words.note: The altar in the Beis HaMikdash where korbanos were brought.

chunks.en: at the rooster's call, or close to it,
chunks.st: at the crow of the rooster or adjacent to it,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says "gever" may also mean a man who called out to wake the Kohanim.

chunks.en: either before it or after it.
chunks.st: whether before it or after it,
chunks.stMore: as there was no insistence on a precise time.

chunks.en: On Yom Kippur, from midnight,
chunks.st: And on Yom Kippur they would remove the ashes earlier, from midnight onward.

chunks.en: and on the Yamim Tovim, from the end of the first watch.
chunks.st: And on the Festivals, the ashes were removed even earlier, at the end of the first watch.

words.note: The night was split into watches, like shifts of guards.

chunks.en: And the rooster's call would not come
chunks.st: And the call of the rooster would not arrive on Festivals

chunks.en: before the courtyard was full of Jews.
chunks.explain: So many people came with korbanos that the Kohanim started early.
chunks.st: until the Temple courtyard was full with the Jewish people who vowed to bring offerings and would fulfill their obligations on the Festivals.
chunks.stMore: Those offerings were sacrificed immediately following the daily offering.

words.note: The azarah, the big courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.
